text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — propose we split private-deploy backlog into three swimlanes: Packaging (installer + airgap), Upgrades (in-place vs rolling), Networking (customer-managed IPAM/peering). Thoughts?
Sophie Li: +1 on swimlanes. can we also add a small "validation" lane for post-upgrade probes and e2e smoke? customers keep asking for a non-blocking rollback signal. :eyes:
Jon Patel: Agreed. For upgrades the big question: do we prioritize zero-downtime rolling for multi-tenant onprem or safe in-place with clear downtime windows? both are heavy.
Raju Menon: For most field customers, network is the blocker — if IPAM is customer-managed we need clear guidance on port requirements and preserved NAT mapping. otherwise installs fail 25% of time.
Alex Gomez: Suggestion: split priority by customer impact + implementability. e.g., P0 = airgap installer reliability (blocks onboarding), P1 = customer IPAM docs + ip-preserve mode, P2 = rolling upgrade automation.
Maria Chen: OK — concrete ask: can @Jon and @Raju sketch minimal acceptance criteria for each swimlane by EOD Thu? we need to present to PM sync Friday.
Jon Patel: I'll do upgrades acceptance criteria. high level:
```
Acceptance - Upgrades:
- can perform single-node rolling with <10% request error budget
- can rollback to previous operator image within 3 mins
- migration path documented for DB schema changes
- non-blocking preflight that validates IP connectivity
```
I'll add measured SLO targets.
Raju Menon: For network: draft checklist I propose: customer IP range validated, ephemeral NAT preserved OR documented NAT change window, DNS entries TTL <= 60s recommended, MGMT plane reachable on ports 22,443,9411. Also include a minimal iptables snippet customers can run.
Sophie Li: Validation lane items (my list): smoke-runner that hits admin + inference endpoints, tokenized workload replay for latency regression check, canary % thresholds and automated cutover script.
Alex Gomez: Also need to be explicit about rollback criteria — e.g., if post-upgrade smoke fails for >2 consecutive nodes, automated rollback triggers. That should be part of the upgrade automation spec.
Maria Chen: One policy question — do we allow customers to opt into "operator-shim" (our agent) auto-upgrade? some legal/customers want manual control. propose default = manual, opt-in auto for Dedicated/enterprise customers.
Jon Patel: Default manual is safer. we'll need a clear opt-in contract for auto upgrades and a UI flag in console.
Raju Menon: Implementation note: opt-in auto-upgrade requires us to support a dry-run mode that reports exactly what will change (images, hooks) and a rollback image pinned in registry. otherwise customers won't sign.
deploy-bot: build/installer:v2.4.0 created for testing — tag: canary-1736002468
Sophie Li: Nice. can we add a short-run plan for one field pilot customer (ACME) that has strict IPAM? if we validate with them we should reduce regressions a lot.
Maria Chen: Action items:
- Jon: upgrades acceptance criteria doc (due Thu EOD)
- Raju: network checklist + iptables snippet (due Thu EOD)
- Sophie: validation harness PR + canary runbook (due Fri noon)
- Alex: backlog swimlane board + initial prioritization (due Fri EOD)
I'll own collecting into a single rollout playbook for the PM sync.
Alex Gomez: I'll create swimlane board and tag items with severity and estimated eng hours.
Jon Patel: One more note: add test case for customers on older kernel versions (4.14/4.19). past failures bite us.
Raju Menon: noted. also flag windows installs as separate constraint — we should not mix in the first pilot.
Sophie Li: :thumbsup: leaving comments on the shared doc now.
Maria Chen: Thanks team — let's reconvene after the deliverables. keeping this thread for the record and to paste into the Friday PM sync notes.
